presentation: English presentation of source tactile images and verbatim model answers. Fixed15-second text replay; inference waits omitted. Not a latency comparison.
selection: These five examples were purposefully selected from a frozen local reconstructed tactile QA test after reviewing Original Qwen and Touch-R1 results, then queried with Astra. They are qualitative examples, not a random benchmark sample or aggregate success-rate estimate.
inputs: Inputs are tactile sensor images / visualizations from GelSight and Tac3D acquisitions, not ordinary camera RGB images. No answer or object name was supplied in the common explanatory prompt.
labels: “Matches source label” indicates agreement with the supplied source annotations. The source property annotations have not been independently physically calibrated. Correct option selection does not independently validate every physical statement in an explanation.
training: Original Qwen and Touch-R1 share the same base model with the task-trained adapter disabled or enabled. Astra is a zero-shot comparison; training budgets are not matched.
resolution: Qwen and Touch-R1 use the default processor limit of 448×448. Astra receives the same source images at high detail; resolutions are not matched.
model_provenance: Astra was requested and returned under the name gpt-6-astra through an existing third-party endpoint; backend identity was not independently attested.

cases.editorial_takeaway: Both baselines select large. Touch-R1 selects small, matching the source label.

cases.actual_prompt:
Which protrusion label is best supported by the tactile evidence?
Return the option letter on the first line. Then give a brief explanation of at most 45 words based on the visible evidence. Do not invent force or displacement measurements. Answer in English.

The maps show a broad, prominent central region with a bright core and extensive surrounding gradients across pressing and sliding. This substantial contact footprint best supports a large protrusion rather than a small bump or no protrusion.

B. small

The grid shows a small, localized area of increased tactile signal intensity.
